title: Quasi-coherent modules under an affine morphism
statement: Let $u:U\to X$ be an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and write $\mathcal A=u_*\mathcal O_U$, a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras through $u^\sharp:\mathcal O_X\to u_*\mathcal O_U$. An *$\mathcal A$-module* is a sheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules on $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], regarded as an $\mathcal O_X$-module through $u^\sharp$; morphisms of $\mathcal A$-modules are the $\mathcal A$-linear maps. An $\mathcal A$-module $\mathcal G$ is *quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal A$-module* if every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $W$ with an exact sequence $\bigoplus_{j\in J}\mathcal A|_W\to\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal A|_W\to\mathcal G|_W\to0$ of $\mathcal A|_W$-modules for some sets $I,J$; quasi-coherence of $\mathcal O_X$- and $\mathcal O_U$-modules is that of [pqf-def-coherent]. For an $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$ the pushforward $u_*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is an $\mathcal A$-module, $\mathcal A(V)=\mathcal O_U(u^{-1}V)$ acting on $(u_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(u^{-1}V)$. Then: (1) an $\mathcal A$-module is quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal A$-module if and only if its underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent; (2) for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$, $u_*\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-module, and $\mathcal F\mapsto u_*\mathcal F$ is an equivalence from the category of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules ($\mathcal O_U$-linear maps) to the category of quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-modules ($\mathcal A$-linear maps); (3) a quasi-inverse is $\mathcal G\mapsto h(\mathcal G)=u^*\mathcal G\otimes_{u^*\mathcal A}\mathcal O_U$, where $u^*$ is the pullback of [def-pc-module-pullback], $u^*\mathcal A=\mathcal O_U\otimes_{u^{-1}\mathcal O_X}u^{-1}\mathcal A$ is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_U$-algebras, $u^*\mathcal G$ is a $u^*\mathcal A$-module through $(b\otimes a)(b'\otimes g)=bb'\otimes ag$, $\mathcal O_U$ is a $u^*\mathcal A$-algebra through the counit $\epsilon:u^*\mathcal A=u^*u_*\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal O_U$, and $\otimes_{u^*\mathcal A}$ is the change of rings of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; precisely, the natural maps $\alpha_{\mathcal F}:h(u_*\mathcal F)\to\mathcal F$ induced by the counit $u^*u_*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ and $\beta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to u_*h(\mathcal G)$ adjoint to $u^*\mathcal G\to h(\mathcal G)$, $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, are isomorphisms of $\mathcal O_U$-modules and of $\mathcal A$-modules respectively.

proof.text: Assertion (1). By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec] (1), $\mathcal A=u_*\mathcal O_U$ is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras whose underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent. The definition of quasi-coherence as an $\mathcal A$-module in the statement is the one of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherence-scalar-restriction] for $S=X$ and this $\mathcal A$, so that lemma gives (1).

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01SB, proof: 'The final statement is Lemma 0H88'

proof.text: The functor. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module. For opens $V'\subseteq V$ of $X$ the $\mathcal O_U(u^{-1}V)$-module structure on $\mathcal F(u^{-1}V)$ is compatible with restriction, so $u_*\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules, and its underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module (through $u^\sharp$) is the pushforward $u_*\mathcal F$ of [def-pc-module-pullback]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] (1) (the morphism $u$ is affine) $u_*\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, hence a quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-module by Step 1. An $\mathcal O_U$-linear $\psi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ gives the $\mathcal A$-linear $u_*\psi$ (components $\psi_{u^{-1}V}$). So $u_*$ is a functor from quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules to quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-modules.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01SB, proof, first paragraph (via Lemma 01S7 and Schemes, Lemma 01LC)

proof.text: The construction $h$ and the two maps. By [def-pc-module-pullback], $u^*\mathcal A=\mathcal O_U\otimes_{u^{-1}\mathcal O_X}u^{-1}\mathcal A$ and $u^*\mathcal G=\mathcal O_U\otimes_{u^{-1}\mathcal O_X}u^{-1}\mathcal G$ are sheafifications of presheaf tensor products; $u^{-1}\mathcal A$ is a sheaf of commutative $u^{-1}\mathcal O_X$-algebras, so $u^*\mathcal A$ is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_U$-algebras, and $(b\otimes a)(b'\otimes g)=bb'\otimes ag$ on the presheaf level makes $u^*\mathcal G$ a $u^*\mathcal A$-module; the unit $\eta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to u_*u^*\mathcal G$ sends $g$ to (the class of) $1\otimes g$, so $\eta_{\mathcal A}(a)\eta_{\mathcal G}(g)=\eta_{\mathcal G}(ag)$ and $\eta_{\mathcal A}$ is multiplicative. The counit $\epsilon:u^*\mathcal A\to\mathcal O_U$ (adjoint to $\mathrm{id}:\mathcal A\to u_*\mathcal O_U$) is $b\otimes a\mapsto b\cdot a$ on the presheaf level, a morphism of $\mathcal O_U$-algebras. Set $h(\mathcal G)=u^*\mathcal G\otimes_{u^*\mathcal A}\mathcal O_U$ (change of rings along $\epsilon$, [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]) and $h(\psi)=u^*\psi\otimes1$ for $\mathcal A$-linear $\psi$; $u^*\psi$ is $u^*\mathcal A$-linear. Quasi-coherence: $\mathcal G$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module by Step 1 and $\mathcal A$ is one by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec] (1), so $u^*\mathcal G$ and $u^*\mathcal A$ are quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]; [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-change-of-rings] with $Y=U$, $\mathcal B=u^*\mathcal A$, $\mathcal C=\mathcal O_U$, $\varphi=\epsilon$, $\mathcal P=u^*\mathcal G$ shows that $h(\mathcal G)$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module and that $t_W:(u^*\mathcal G)(W)\otimes_{(u^*\mathcal A)(W)}\mathcal O_U(W)\to h(\mathcal G)(W)$ is bijective for every affine open $W\subseteq U$. The maps: for a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$, regard $\mathcal F$ as a $u^*\mathcal A$-module through $\epsilon$; the counit $\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}:u^*u_*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is $u^*\mathcal A$-linear (on the presheaf level it is $b\otimes s\mapsto b\cdot s$, and $(b\otimes a)(b'\otimes s)=bb'\otimes as\mapsto bb'as=\epsilon(b\otimes a)\cdot(b's)$), so by the universal property of the sectionwise tensor product and of sheafification it induces the $\mathcal O_U$-linear $\alpha_{\mathcal F}:h(u_*\mathcal F)\to\mathcal F$, $p\otimes c\mapsto c\cdot\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}(p)$. For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-module $\mathcal G$ let $\gamma:u^*\mathcal G\to h(\mathcal G)$, $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, and $\beta_{\mathcal G}=u_*(\gamma)\circ\eta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to u_*h(\mathcal G)$, an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map with $\beta_{\mathcal G}(g)=\eta_{\mathcal G}(g)\otimes1$. Both are natural in $\mathcal F$, resp. $\mathcal G$, because the counit, the unit and $\gamma$ are.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01SB, proof, second paragraph (construction of h and 'Elucidation')

proof.text: Sections over $u^{-1}(V)$. Let $V\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $W=u^{-1}(V)$, which is affine because $u$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], $R=\mathcal O_X(V)$, $B=\mathcal O_U(W)=\mathcal A(V)$, $\rho=u^\sharp_V:R\to B$. For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal H$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] (with $f=u$ and the affine opens $V$ and $W\subseteq u^{-1}V$) gives the $B$-linear bijection $c_{\mathcal H}:\mathcal H(V)\otimes_RB\to(u^*\mathcal H)(W)$, $s\otimes b\mapsto b\cdot\eta_{\mathcal H}(s)|_W$. For $\mathcal H=\mathcal A$: $c_{\mathcal A}$ is a ring isomorphism $B\otimes_RB\to(u^*\mathcal A)(W)$, since $c_{\mathcal A}(a\otimes b)c_{\mathcal A}(a'\otimes b')=bb'\eta_{\mathcal A}(a)\eta_{\mathcal A}(a')=bb'\eta_{\mathcal A}(aa')=c_{\mathcal A}(aa'\otimes bb')$ (Step 3), and $\epsilon_W\circ c_{\mathcal A}$ is the multiplication $\mu:B\otimes_RB\to B$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, because $\epsilon(\eta_{\mathcal A}(a))=a$ (Step 3). For $\mathcal H=\mathcal G$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-module (quasi-coherent over $\mathcal O_X$ by Step 1), $N=\mathcal G(V)$ is a $B$-module and, again by $\eta_{\mathcal A}(a)\eta_{\mathcal G}(g)=\eta_{\mathcal G}(ag)$, $c_{\mathcal G}$ carries the $B\otimes_RB$-module structure $(b_1\otimes b_2)(n\otimes b)=b_1n\otimes b_2b$ on $N\otimes_RB$ to the $(u^*\mathcal A)(W)$-module structure of $(u^*\mathcal G)(W)$. With the bijection $t_W$ of Step 3 we get a bijection $\kappa_{\mathcal G}:(N\otimes_RB)\otimes_{B\otimes_RB}B\to h(\mathcal G)(W)$, $(n\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto t_W(c_{\mathcal G}(n\otimes b)\otimes c)$, where $B$ is a $B\otimes_RB$-algebra through $\mu$; it is $B$-linear for the action of $B=\mathcal O_U(W)$ on the last factor.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01SB, proof: 'This may be checked on the members of an affine covering, i.e., when X and S are affine'

proof.text: The algebra identity. Let $\rho:R\to B$ be a ring map, $N$ a $B$-module, $N\otimes_RB$ the $B\otimes_RB$-module with $(b_1\otimes b_2)(n\otimes b)=b_1n\otimes b_2b$, and $B$ a $B\otimes_RB$-algebra through $\mu(b_1\otimes b_2)=b_1b_2$. Then $\theta:(N\otimes_RB)\otimes_{B\otimes_RB}B\to N$, $(n\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto bc\,n$, is a well-defined isomorphism, $B$-linear for the action on the last factor, with inverse $n\mapsto(n\otimes1)\otimes1$. Well defined: $(n,b,c)\mapsto bcn$ is $R$-balanced in $(n,b)$ and additive in each variable, and for $x=b_1\otimes b_2$ both $(x(n\otimes b))\otimes c=(b_1n\otimes b_2b)\otimes c\mapsto b_2bc\,b_1n$ and $(n\otimes b)\otimes\mu(x)c\mapsto b\,b_1b_2c\,n$ agree. $\theta((n\otimes1)\otimes1)=n$. Conversely $(n\otimes b)\otimes c=((1\otimes b)(n\otimes1))\otimes c=(n\otimes1)\otimes bc$ and $(bc\,n\otimes1)\otimes1=((bc\otimes1)(n\otimes1))\otimes1=(n\otimes1)\otimes bc$, so $(\theta((n\otimes b)\otimes c)\otimes1)\otimes1=(n\otimes b)\otimes c$ on generators. $B$-linearity on the last factor: $\theta((n\otimes b)\otimes c'c)=bc'c\,n=c'\theta((n\otimes b)\otimes c)$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01SB, proof: 'the key algebra observation ... (N tensor_R A) tensor_{(A tensor_R A)} A = N ... We omit the details' (details written by the agent)

proof.text: $\alpha_{\mathcal F}$ is an isomorphism. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module and $\mathcal G=u_*\mathcal F$ (quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-module by Step 2). For an affine open $V\subseteq X$ with $W=u^{-1}V$, $N=\mathcal G(V)=\mathcal F(W)$. By the triangle identity $u_*(\varepsilon_{\mathcal F})\circ\eta_{u_*\mathcal F}=\mathrm{id}$ we have $\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}(\eta_{u_*\mathcal F}(n)|_W)=n$, so by Steps 3 and 4 $(\alpha_{\mathcal F})_W\circ\kappa_{\mathcal G}((n\otimes b)\otimes c)=c\cdot\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}(b\cdot\eta(n)|_W)=bc\,n=\theta((n\otimes b)\otimes c)$. As $\kappa_{\mathcal G}$ and $\theta$ (Step 5) are bijective, $(\alpha_{\mathcal F})_W$ is bijective. If $V$ runs over an affine open cover of $X$, the opens $u^{-1}V$ form an affine open cover of $U$; $h(u_*\mathcal F)$ and $\mathcal F$ are quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules (Step 3), so [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-iso-on-affine-cover] shows that $\alpha_{\mathcal F}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01SB, proof, last two paragraphs

proof.text: $\beta_{\mathcal G}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal A$-modules. Let $\mathcal G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-module, $V\subseteq X$ affine open, $W=u^{-1}V$, $N=\mathcal G(V)$. By Steps 3 and 4, $(\beta_{\mathcal G})_V(n)=t_W(\eta_{\mathcal G}(n)|_W\otimes1)=\kappa_{\mathcal G}((n\otimes1)\otimes1)=\kappa_{\mathcal G}(\theta^{-1}(n))$, a bijection $N\to h(\mathcal G)(W)=(u_*h(\mathcal G))(V)$ by Steps 4 and 5. $\mathcal G$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module (Step 1), $u_*h(\mathcal G)$ is one by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] (1) applied to the quasi-coherent $h(\mathcal G)$ (Step 3), and $\beta_{\mathcal G}$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear; [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-iso-on-affine-cover] applied to the cover of $X$ by all affine opens shows that $\beta_{\mathcal G}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. It is $\mathcal A$-linear: for $a\in\mathcal A(V)=B$ and $n\in N$, $(\beta_{\mathcal G})_V(an)=\kappa_{\mathcal G}(\theta^{-1}(an))=\kappa_{\mathcal G}(a\cdot\theta^{-1}(n))=a\cdot(\beta_{\mathcal G})_V(n)$, using the $B$-linearity of $\theta$ and of $\kappa_{\mathcal G}$ for the action on the last factor, which is the action of $\mathcal A(V)=\mathcal O_U(W)$ on $(u_*h(\mathcal G))(V)$; for an arbitrary open $V'$, $a\in\mathcal A(V')$, $g\in\mathcal G(V')$, the sections $\beta(ag)$ and $a\beta(g)$ agree on every affine open $V\subseteq V'$, hence are equal since affine opens form a basis and $u_*h(\mathcal G)$ is a sheaf. An $\mathcal A$-linear map that is bijective on all sections has an $\mathcal A$-linear inverse.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01SB, proof, last two paragraphs

proof.text: Conclusion. By Step 2, $u_*$ is a functor from quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules to quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-modules; by Step 3, $h$ is a functor in the other direction (each $h(\mathcal G)$ quasi-coherent); by Steps 6 and 7 the natural transformations $\alpha:h\circ u_*\to\mathrm{id}$ and $\beta:\mathrm{id}\to u_*\circ h$ are natural isomorphisms. Hence $u_*$ is an equivalence with quasi-inverse $h$, which is (2) and (3).
